headline_marked: [[HSC and equivalent exam results published today]], over 1.27 million candidates registered
headline: HSC and equivalent exam results published today, over 1.27 million candidates registered
summary: Students can check their results online, via SMS, or directly from their educational institutions following the formal announcement at 11:00 AM.
details: The results of this year  HSC and equivalent examinations are being published today. The formal announcement program began at 11:00 AM at the International Mother Language Institute in Dhaka.

Students can access their results online through eduboardresults.gov.bd or educationboardresults.gov.bd, or their respective education board websites. They need to select the examination, board, year (2026), and enter their roll and registration numbers.

Alternatively, results can be checked via SMS by sending "HSC <Board_initials> <Roll_number> 2026" to 16140. Educational institutions can also download result sheets using their EIIN and students can collect results directly from them.

A total of 12,70,583 candidates registered for this year  HSC and equivalent examinations under 11 education boards. The results were initially scheduled for October 29 but were rescheduled to October 31.
Students wishing to have their results re-evaluated can apply online from November 1 to 7. Details regarding the application process will be available on the respective education boards  websites.

headline_marked: [[Motorcycle recovered in ex-airman Tahsif Souri case]]; friend claims chase led to river jump
headline: Motorcycle recovered in ex-airman Tahsif Souri case; friend claims chase led to river jump
summary: The Police Bureau of Investigation seized a black motorcycle from Tongi, based on information from Tahsif's friend, Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip. Dip told investigators he and Tahsif were chased, leading Tahsif to jump into the Turag River.
details: The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) yesterday recovered a motorcycle from Mazar Basti in Tongi, about three kilometres from where the body of former airman KM Tahsif Souri was found in the Turag River.

Investigators are yet to establish if the black motorcycle belongs to the 28-year-old Tahsif or is the same one he was seen riding when he left home on Tuesday evening, as captured in CCTV footage. The bike was seized based on information provided by Tahsif’s friend, Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip.

Dip, whom Tahsif's family described as being like a younger brother, told investigators that he and Tahsif were chased by some people in the Mazar Basti area. While fleeing, Tahsif reportedly jumped into the Turag River, but Dip managed to escape.

Additional Deputy Inspector General Enayet Rahman Manna of PBI’s Dhaka Metro North stated that all information provided by Dip is being cross-checked, as they do not believe everything he says outright. The recovered motorcycle's connection to the case is still unverified.

Regarding Dip's statement of being chased, a PBI official mentioned Dip claimed they ran after seeing two police officers. However, Tahsif’s father, AKM Enayetul Karim, dismissed Dip’s claim as "absurd," stating a defence officer would not run from the police.

Tahsif, a former Bangladesh Air Force flight lieutenant, left his Uttara home on Tuesday evening and did not return. River police recovered his body from the Turag near Rajabari Ghat in Uttarkhan on Wednesday afternoon.

Tahsif's name came into the limelight following allegations that he had circulated a video clip purportedly showing ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina leaving the country by aircraft on August 5, 2024.

PBI took Dip into custody from his Mohammadpur house early yesterday. A local tea stall owner, Jubaida Begum, reported noticing a motorcycle without a number plate parked in the Mazar Basti area since Wednesday morning.

PBI investigators are examining the circumstances of why Tahsif and Dip visited the area around 2:00 AM, using technological evidence to verify Dip's statements and movements. Dip reportedly returned home after 2:30 AM on Wednesday.

Additional Inspector General of River Police Md Rezaul Karim confirmed they have contacted Tahsif’s family multiple times. The family is considering filing a case, and police will proceed if they do not do so soon.
